blocking.title: AI nuclear use is too rare to be seen, and still not credible: strikes in 2 of 14 unaided 30-year worlds (4 in 420 world-years) while 4 to 6 nations hold 132 to 156 warheads and ballistic missiles; on seeds 1 to 10 the builder's PLAN 7.3g sweep had 4 of 10 seeds and 21 decisions, at HEAD 2 of 10 and 4; all 4 strikes are by the Soviet Union, on the same Dutch point a year apart (734,042 and 566,582 dead) and twice on South Africa, none answered; God-set France (overrun, fighting to the death, 6 warheads, missiles) strikes once and then holds 5 warheads for 49 days
blocking.fix: Find why the strike rate halved since 7.3g (the stockpile cap, the 6.12a/f threat test, desperation in real wars). A nuclear power losing a war for its life should reach for the bomb in a visible share of games. Aim at the enemy at the front or its core, not twice at one Dutch city a year apart or at South Africa. Let the struck answer, and let a nation that struck once and keeps losing strike again.

blocking.fix: Profile the slow invasionAi calls (src/sim/ai/invasion.ts, the landing plan of a nation at war with no land front) in a war with no land front (Poland against Denmark in 1967 here); their cost grows with the years and the formations. Cache or bound the landing search, and hold the late-game tick to budget, not only seed 99's year 1.
